To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of the lymphatic mapping and sentinel lymphadenectomy technique in patients with breast cancer is safe and effective.

The use of the 3.1.1.1 method of lymphoscintigraphy and sentinel lymph node biopsy for breast cancer is safe and reliable, and that the sentinel nodes can be reliably identified and removed in the axilla regardless of tumor location in the breast.
The lymphatic drainage of breast cancer is not dependent on the tumor location within the glandular tissue, but rather on its location within the quadrant.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of the lymphoscintigraphy in the detection of sentinel nodes in breast cancer.
the development of a new, noninvasive imaging technique that can be used to assess lymphatic drainage of sentinel lymph nodes.
the development of a new, reliable method for the identification of the sentinel lymph node (SLN) in patients with breast cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the sentinel node technique is the most accurate and reliable method for axillary staging in early breast cancer and is now accepted worldwide.
sentinel lymph node biopsy is a reliable method of staging breast cancer, with a low false negative rate, regardless of the location of the tumor within the breast.

the use of sentinel lymph node biopsy is safe and accurate for the axilla and is the standard of care in the United States and in most of Europe for the management of patients with clinically node-negative breast carcinoma.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the sentinel lymph node biopsy (SLNB) is a reliable technique for the detection of metastatic disease within the axilla.
the lymphatic drainage from the breast to the axillary sentinel lymph node (SLN) is not affected by tumor location in the breast.
the lymphatic drainage of breast tumors is unpredictable and that the lymphatic system does not follow a predictable pattern of flow.

we can now reliably predict lymph node metastasis in patients with breast cancer, and we can do it using a single lymph node, the sentinel lymph node (SLN), which can be obtained by using a simple and minimally invasive procedure.
the lymph nodes are not a reliable indicator of cancer spread.
